title: Pair texts only for a named purpose
statement: Pair two texts only for a named comparison or synthesis purpose, not merely to set them side by side.
detail: Three reading-course packages state it. A Grade 5 course plan's case for review lists, as resolved for bounded plan review, that paired-text placements name a shared comparison or synthesis purpose rather than merely placing two texts together. The Grade 4 and Grade 6 generation contracts define paired texts as two related but separate texts, such as a poem beside an informational passage, read and compared, not one passage with an inserted stanza. It is a planning rule the packages adopted, not an outcome measured with learners.

evidence.quote: Paired-text placements name a shared comparison or synthesis purpose rather than merely placing two texts together.
Paired texts are two related but ultimately separate texts.
**Paired texts are two separate texts** (e.g. a poem beside an informational passage), related by theme,
read and compared — not one passage with an inserted stanza.
